issues.description: Data.dta is the required analysis input and is absent from the imported package inventory. The datasheet identifies the underlying field-site data as proprietary and not publicly available, but it does not establish that authorized access is impossible. The file's actual schema, period, and coverage therefore remain unverified.

The supplied Stata entry program reads an already assembled Data.dta; it does not show how field-site records become that file. The datasheet says raw-data manipulations were programmatic, and OA.2 describes text-derived controls using jieba and gensim, but this archive contains no separate preparation program or Data.dta. An author-prepared Data.dta is a valid primary input; if only raw site records are offered, the missing preparation code/schema needs clarification.

dependency_review.description: The frozen checklist edge is a mandatory read: CCY_Code.do loads Data.dta at its opening and reloads it for table 7.

actions.description: Request the author-prepared Data.dta used by CCY_Code.do through the authors' permitted access process. The datasheet says the field-site data are proprietary and not public, but no explicit denial was observed. Ask the authors to confirm this is the analysis-ready file and to state its record period, unit, and the consumed fields, including the employee_* family.
steps: Request the author-prepared Data.dta from the authors or research site using an authorized channel; do not substitute public data.
Confirm the file is the analysis-ready input used by the supplied program, and document its observational unit, record period, expected columns, and any conditions on its use.
Keep any received input in a separate portable working copy alongside CCY_Code.do; preserve the original package and audit files.
validation: After authorized receipt, use a bounded DTA metadata/readability check to verify the exact consumed columns and actual location.
Confirm the period and coverage with the data owner; a bounded header check alone cannot establish full historical or population coverage.

actions.description: Clarify whether author-prepared Data.dta is the intended primary input. If the authors offer only raw field-site records, request the supplied preprocessing program or a complete field/schema and transformation specification that produces the variables used by the Stata tables, including the text-derived controls. The appendix's textual recipe alone does not establish the input-to-file mapping.
steps: Ask the authors to confirm whether Data.dta is already the complete analysis-ready file for tables 1–7.
If not, obtain the author-supplied preparation code and schema for the raw field-site inputs; preserve its stated text segmentation, embedding settings, filters, and variable mappings.
Treat a compatible author-prepared Data.dta as the primary input when available; do not independently rebuild the research data from the appendix description.
validation: Compare the confirmed prepared-file schema with the program's consumed variable list and the employee_* wildcard expansion.
If a preparation program is supplied later, review its exact inputs and output contract before proposing any code or data substitution.

actions.description: If and only if the authorized raw-to-Data.dta preparation path is required, set up compatible jieba and gensim distributions in the available Python 3.12 environment after the authors provide the preparation code or exact interface requirements. Their installed metadata is absent here. These packages are not needed to run CCY_Code.do with a compatible author-prepared Data.dta.
steps: Do not install packages during this assessment.
If authors confirm the raw-data construction route, install or select the author-compatible jieba and gensim versions in an authorized working environment and preserve the recorded versions.
validation: After the preparation code is provided, verify only package metadata and documented API compatibility; do not run a Word2Vec fit until a separate authorized execution step.

actions.description: After authorized Data.dta is received and its consumed variables are verified, run the supplied CCY_Code.do unchanged from a separate portable working directory with Stata 18 and eststo, estpost, and esttab available. The source order is: open a time-stamped log; load Data.dta and produce Table 1 summaries; drop city2id == 2 and run Tables 2–5; apply msgnumvisittosign > 2 for Table 6; reload Data.dta, drop city2id == 2, and run Table 7 employee fixed-effect models; close the log. Output is captured in the current working directory's time-stamped Stata log. StataCorp's automatic-memory documentation says the legacy set memory line is ignored; no edit is needed for that line.
steps: Create a separate portable working copy of CCY_Code.do; place the authorized, verified Data.dta in the same working directory because both use statements are relative.
Use the registered Stata 18 runtime with eststo, estpost, and esttab available; keep the source script and analysis data in the working copy, not in the audit generation.
Run the do-file top to bottom so the table 7 re-read starts from the original Data.dta after the table 6 filter.
Retain the resulting time-stamped Stata log and review all tables 1–7; do not overwrite the original package or supplied log.
validation: Before launch, confirm the required DTA columns and exact relative location with a bounded metadata check.
After an authorized run, review the fresh log for completion through the final log close and compare table outputs with the authors' documented main-table target.

review_notes: The assessed target is the supplied Stata analysis driver for the main tables 1–7. The online appendix title matches the frozen paper title; additional supplementary robustness sections are contextual to this supplied-code target because no other analysis entry program is included in the package inventory.

Data.dta is required and absent from the imported package inventory. The datasheet describes the field-site data as proprietary and not publicly available, but no access denial was established. The file's actual schema, record period, and coverage remain unverified.

The appendix describes text-based controls using jieba and gensim. Their distribution metadata is absent in this environment; they are needed only if the raw-to-Data.dta preparation route is pursued, not for the supplied Stata driver when the compatible author-prepared dataset is available.

Stata 18, eststo, estpost, and esttab have metadata availability evidence. StataCorp documents that legacy set memory commands are ignored under automatic memory management; that compatibility inference is not a blocker or an edit proposal.

No standard commercial database or author-named public data product is identified as a required input, so the frozen common commercial-resource catalog has no applicable required product to resolve. The only empirical input named in the datasheet is proprietary field-site data.
Two failed exact Stata 18 manual-PDF fetches are retained as unreferenced process-history inspection artifacts; they returned no page content and support no compatibility conclusion.
The byte-first appendix screen withheld candidate line 158 in full before display; it was not followed or used as evidence. Its inspection row is process-only and unused in all evidence_ids arrays.
No author code, empirical dataset, package module, or model payload has been executed or loaded; execution remains unverified.
